title: Configure pySpark join to handle bucketed datasets
question:
Apache Spark 3.2:
I have 2 bucketed datasets in parquet files, bucketed with the same column (visitor_id) and same amount of buckets (1024)
I would like to join them and my question is, how can i configure the join in such a way that Spark is aware of the bucketing and it omits the shuffling? I ask this because in the output of "explain()" command, i still see BroadcastExchange (see steps 7 and 8 below) which should not happen in bucketed data.

from py4j.java_gateway import java_import
java_import(spark._sc._jvm, "org.apache.spark.sql.api.python.*")
path_1="s3://PATH1/*.parquet"
path_2="s3://PATH2/*.parquet"
df_1 = spark.read.parquet(path_1)
df_2 = spark.read.parquet(path_2)
joined = df_1.join(df_2, 'visitor_id')
joined.explain('formatted'):

The output as you know is huge so i only show the relevant steps.

(4) Scan parquet 
(5) Filter
(6) Project
(7) BroadcastExchange
(8) BroadcastHashJoin
(9) Project
answer:
Spark bucketing only works when data is written and read as a table.

Try something like this

numBuckets = 10
(df_1
    .write
    .format("parquet")
    .bucketBy(numBuckets, "visitor_id")
    .option("path", "/path/to/your/table1")
    .saveAsTable("TABLE1")
)
(df_2
    .write
    .format("parquet")
    .bucketBy(numBuckets, "visitor_id")
    .option("path", "/path/to/your/table2")
    .saveAsTable("TABLE2")
)

df_1 = (
    spark
    .read
    .option("path", "/path/to/your/table1")
    .table("TABLE1")
)
df_2 = (
    spark
    .read
    .option("path", "/path/to/your/table2")
    .table("TABLE2")
)

joined = df_1.join(df_2, 'visitor_id')
